text:
maria: Heads up — onboarding customer T-9821 is hitting a bunch of 429s from our Dedicated pool. They reported bursty traffic during onboarding tests and say autoscale didn’t relieve the backlog. Can someone check per-tenant quota/denom?

devon: Which pool and tenant ID? any screenshots of the 429s?

maria: Tenant T-9821, reserved pool: eu-west-2-reserved-03. Customer sent trace showing immediate 429s after a sequence of short requests. Link to trace: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/T-9821/eu-west-2/1779004300

ops-bot: Alert: dedicated-reserved-pool eu-west-2-reserved-03 reported 95% queue depth for tenant T-9821 between 2026-03-17T10:05Z and 2026-03-17T10:12Z. Relevant logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T10:05:21Z] svc:inference runtime:accept request tenant=T-9821 seq=45 latency=18ms
[2026-03-17T10:05:21Z] svc:quota allow=false tenant=T-9821 reason=rate_limit_exceeded key=tenant:T-9821:rate_unit
[2026-03-17T10:05:22Z] svc:enqueue queue_len=128 pool=eu-west-2-reserved-03
[2026-03-17T10:05:23Z] svc:autoscaler warmup_in_progress pool=eu-west-2-reserved-03 warmup_remaining=1780s
```

sree: I pulled the tenant quota config for T-9821 via admin API. Looks like a denom/unit mismatch — the plan was converted and the denom is set to "MINUTES" instead of "HOURS", which massively reduced allowed sustained rate. Snippet: 
```
{ "tenant_id": "T-9821", "plan": "onboard-pro", "rate_limit": "18000", "rate_unit": "MINUTES", "burst": "1200" }
```
This effectively means 18k units per minute -> logic in quota service mistakenly interprets denom as per-minute but our billing plan intended per-hour. During conversion someone applied the plan multiplier incorrectly.

emma: Oof. If service thinks it's per-minute we hit limit fast. Two immediate remediation options: 1) temporary support override to bump the tenant's effective units to match intended hours OR 2) flip the unit back to HOURS and restart quota sync (low-risk). Which do we want for fastest customer relief?

devon: Can ops do a one-off override? I can patch the migration script after we stabilize.

sree: Admin API allows an ephemeral override: 
```
POST /admin/v1/tenants/T-9821/overrides
{ "rate_limit": "18000", "rate_unit": "HOURS", "expires_at": "2026-03-20T00:00:00Z" }
```
I ran a dry-run to confirm effect — it would drop their 429s based on the sim.

simon: Also worth noting autoscaler warmup is configured to be conservative for reserved pools: we have min_replica_warmup_seconds=1800 and the pool was still in warmup from a recent node recycle. Even with a quota fix, warmup delays could keep latency high for a few minutes. We should coordinate: override quota now, restart pool warmup flag to allow faster scale (set warmup_remaining to 60s), then revert if needed.

maria: Customer is on a tight onboarding timeline. Please proceed with override and warmup tweak; I'll notify them.

emma: On it — applying override now and bumping warmup.

ops-bot: ACTION LOG: override.created by emma for tenant T-9821 at 2026-03-17T10:27:10Z, expires 2026-03-20T00:00:00Z. autoscaler.warmup_override applied by emma: pool=eu-west-2-reserved-03 warmup_remaining=60s

sree: Observability shows 429 rate dropping within 45s of override. Sample metric pre/post: 
```
tenant.T-9821.429_rate: before=72/min after=3/min
queue.depth.pool=eu-west-2-reserved-03: before=118 after=14
latency.p95: before=1.6s after=420ms
```

devon: Created a follow-up ticket to revert the temporary overrides once migration script is patched: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7129

maria: Customer confirmed onboarding tests passed post-fix. Closing escalation but leaving the ticket open for migration patch. Thanks team :tada:

sree: Root cause: migration denom mismatch (MINUTES vs HOURS) + coincident autoscaler warmup from recent node recycle -> compounded impact. Remediation: patch migration conversion, add unit validation in quota import, add an alert when warmup_remaining > configured and queue depth > threshold.

emma: I'll own the patch and the validation. Assigning INF-7130 to me.

maria: Great—closing thread. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :heart:
